title: POC scope & model evaluation briefing - Polyglot Insights
topics: deployment mode - hosted vs dedicated vs VPC
summary: Kickoff scoping for a multilingual POC focused on extraction + summarization for customer support tickets in 10 languages. Discussed shortlist of open models, target QPS and latency SLOs, dataset slice for evals, proposal for 3-week bench program, and next steps to run initial benchmarks on Redwood hosted infra. Key risks: tokenization variance across languages and prompt robustness to domain jargon.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-15 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), María (Polyglot Head ML), Tomasz (Eng Manager), Sana (NLP researcher), Eric (Infra)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — I'm Alex Morton, I'll run the POC coordination. Priya's on for the model side. Jonah will help with infra questions.
[00:18] María: Hi all, María here. Excited to get this scoped, we need something fast for our support summarization pipeline across Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, Chinese and Japanese.
[00:30] Priya: Great, could you remind us of your success criteria — like what metrics you care about? Is it F1 on extraction, ROUGE for summary, latency thresholds?
[00:42] Tomasz: Yeah so the hard constraints are: 95th latency under 1.2s for short replies (<=256 tokens) and throughput around 70 qps for the daytime window. Quality we care most about is entity extraction recall (we need recall > 0.92 on named entities from tickets) and summary coherence for non-English languages.
[01:03] Sana: Also domain coverage — we have telecom and fintech jargon that breaks a lot of base models, so robustness matters.
[01:12] Alex: Noted. For the POC we're proposing a 3-week bench + evaluation cycle: week 1 run baseline benchmarks across a shortlist, week 2 fine-tune or prompt-tune if needed and run multilingual stress tests, week 3 integrate into your sandbox and run end-to-end latency and cost estimates. Is that timeline aligned?
[01:28] María: That sounds good. Can we compress to 2 weeks if the first run looks promising?
[01:34] Priya: Possibly, yes — if results meet your thresholds. We'll recommend a primary and fallback model for production.
[01:40] Eric: A couple infra notes: we need to keep all logs in our VPC, and keys in our KMS. SOC2 is required, and we'll need audit logs retained for 1 year. Can Redwood support that in a POC?
[01:55] Jonah: Yes — for the POC we can run on Redwood hosted with VPC peering into your environment or spin up a private Dedicated instance depending on the data residency you want. For audit logs we stream them to your S3/Kafka. There might be minor onboarding friction with certs.
[02:10] Tomasz: Cost wise — we want to understand unit token cost at 70 qps with our batching patterns (most requests ~180 tokens).
[02:19] Priya: We'll capture a few throughput scenarios: 70 qps steady, a 2x burst to 140 qps, and a low-volume 5 qps background. We'll include batching simulation and KV/prefix caching to estimate real unit costs.
[02:33] María: About models — we'd prefer open models due to license and latency. Our internal team has experience with Mistral, Llama-family models and a couple of MPT variants. We are open to smaller LLMs if they meet recall targets.
[02:47] Alex: Our proposed shortlist: Mistral-instruct-34B (quantized), Llama-3-13B-instruct, Falcon-40B-instruct if we need a bigger one, and MPT-30B for a lighter baseline. We'll also run RedPajama-incarnation (RedPajama-INCITE 70B) on a couple of tests for cross-checking. Priya: we might throw in a distilled 7B in the long tail for throughput numbers.
[03:10] Sana: Quick flag — tokenization differences for Chinese/Japanese mean that the effective input length is smaller; we should use language-specific tokenization metrics in the bench.
[03:20] Priya: Absolutely; we'll produce per-language tokenization profiles. For quality we'll run entity extraction F1, summary ROUGE-L, and human evaluation on a ~200-case stratified sample across languages.
[03:33] María: What's the expected compute footprint? We need to know memory requirements to estimate Dedicated capacity.
[03:40] Jonah: Rough ballpark: Llama-3-13B quantized Q4_K8 (example) will run ~40-90 ms per token on A100-type hardware with good batching; Falcon-40B is heavier and needs more memory, likely requires larger instance types. We'll provide GPU-hour estimates per model and per workload.
[04:00] Tomasz: Also, do you support KV cache pinning and prefix caching? Our product reuses conversation prefixes heavily which affects warm cache speed.
[04:10] Priya: Yes, Redwood runtime supports KV cache reuse and prefix caching; we'll instrument cache hit rates in the bench to show how much cost drops if you have high reuse.
[04:18] María: For evaluation datasets — we can provide a 10k sample of anonymized tickets across languages, but for the bench do you want a smaller stratified slice?
[04:27] Alex: Send a 1k stratified slice first (100 per language prioritized by issue type). We'll need labels for named entities and ground truth summaries for the human eval set.
[04:36] Sana: We'll prepare labeling guidance; can Redwood host an evaluation UI or do we need to set up an internal review pipeline?
[04:44] Priya: We have a lightweight eval harness (spreadsheet + diffs) we can share, and a small UI for human raters if you want Redwood to host the eval (permissioned access). For confidentiality we can run the human eval inside your VPC as well.
[04:58] María: Licensing question — if we use Llama-3, are there any commercial restrictions?
[05:04] Alex: We'll surface license notes for each model in the shortlist. Llama-3 variants have Meta licensing; some MPT/Mistral models are permissive but check weights. We'll add a model-licensing appendix to the bench report.
[05:15] Tomasz: Bench specifics — can you include token-level latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), per-model memory, and cost per 1M tokens?
[05:24] Priya: Yes, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput QPS, GPU utilization, warm vs cold start, and cost per 1M tokens across batching scenarios. We'll also annotate where quantization affects quality.
[05:35] María: What about A/B testing during POC? We'd like to run an A/B of your top two models in a canary in prod-like traffic.
[05:43] Alex: We can do a canary on Redwood Dedicated or Hosted with traffic split. If you need full VPC isolation we'll use a private deployment. The POC will recommend the deployment mode by the end.
[05:53] Eric: Security checklist — SSO, SAML, RBAC, encryption at rest with our KMS, and audit log retention. You mentioned streaming logs to our S3; can we get sample ACLs/config?
[06:05] Jonah: We'll send the onboarding checklist and a sample Terraform snippet for VPC peering and S3 log sink.
[06:14] Alex: Ok, quick recap of deliverables and owners...
[06:18] Priya: Action items: baseline bench run on hosted infra against the 4 shortlisted models, per-language token profiles, extraction and summary metrics, cost-estimates, and a proposal for dedicated sizing if needed.
[06:32] María: Good, and what do you need from us to start?
[06:35] Alex: We'll need the 1k stratified sample, an access point for logs if you want us to pull telemetry, and a brief list of must-have entities for extraction. Also confirm preferred languages and priority order.
[06:47] Sana: We'll get the sample and entity list by Friday.
[06:50] Tomasz: And can you share an initial estimate for Dedicated monthly cost if we need reserved capacity for 70 qps?
[06:58] Alex: We'll include a rough sizing estimate in the bench deck and a more precise quote after the initial runs.
[07:06] María: Fine, thanks. Let's aim to start the bench on Monday.
[07:10] Alex: Sounds good — we'll email the kickoff plan and upload the bench-run spreadsheet. Thanks everyone.
[07:17] End of meeting.
